public_question: Is the first liquid out of an espresso puck weak because water only just entered, or can it already be near-saturated?
headline: The first liquid out of this espresso puck was already about 97% as concentrated as the peak.
plain_language_finding: In one pressure-controlled, fraction-resolved dataset, the earliest measured fraction was already ~97% of the peak TDS. This separates WETTING time (water crossing the puck) from DISSOLUTION speed (coffee going into solution) — the liquid can take time to appear while becoming chemically concentrated almost immediately.
uncertainty_or_sensitivity: The first fraction has only ONE replicate; the 23 s boulder-diffusion timescale is the comparator that near-instant dissolution beats — favouring rapid dissolution in this configuration.
validity_range: One rig, one coffee, one configuration (pressure-controlled).
primary_caveat: One rig/config and a single first-fraction replicate — a strong prompt for replication, NOT a universal law. Do not claim all espresso reaches full strength instantly.
practical_implication: Collect TIMED FRACTIONS rather than judging extraction from the final cup; do not assume the first drops are chemically weak.
reproduction: python -c "from puckworks.harness import dissolution_speed_test as f; print(f())"

dependencies.role: the measured 5 s TDS fractions this claim is computed from
supplies the boulder-timescale comparison the finding is stated against

evidence.scope: Extraction yield EY (%) via two internal accounting routes plus an inventory upper bound, all computed from the simulation and module constants.

EY(t) morphology (monotonicity, first-half vs second-half rate), fraction of final yield by t=15 s, plateau band, and the sign of the EY-vs-t_shot relation across the grind sweep vs smrke's digitized Fig-3 curve.

dependencies.role: computes the reported fraction and its comparison

evidence_selections.claim_observable: boulder-scale diffusion timescale (s), the comparator the measured first-fraction concentration is read against
evidence_selections.claim_domain: the cited boulder radius and bath conditions of the source model
evidence_selections.rationale: The reported 97 % is MEASURED from the Waszkiewicz fractions; cameron2020 supplies only the ~23 s comparator, and the conservation gate is what licenses using its internal accounting for that timescale. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: gate_smrke2024_fast_extraction_shape, an independent-external record with a NEGATIVE outcome about EY(t) MORPHOLOGY. That is a different observable from the diffusion timescale and this claim asserts nothing about it; under the previous scheme it nonetheless entered this claim's profile.

evidence_profile.scope: Extraction yield EY (%) via two internal accounting routes plus an inventory upper bound, all computed from the simulation and module constants.

public_question: When a flow curve dips and recovers, does that prove the coffee bed changed (swelling, channeling, fines)?
headline: A machine-and-wetting model can produce a flow dip with no extraction-driven bed change — though it does not reproduce the published flow curve quantitatively — while some traces DO need a time-varying bed.
plain_language_finding: A machine-and-wetting model (pump + headspace + a sharp wetting front advancing into a dry bed, with no extraction-driven change in bed structure) can reproduce a dip-and-recovery, so that shape alone is not a diagnosis. Separately, on a 9-bar rising-flow trace, every constant baseline fails and a time-varying porosity trajectory reconstructs it ~4.9x better — time variation IS needed there (though a flexible non-mechanistic curve does as well, so this does not identify a specific bed mechanism).
uncertainty_or_sensitivity: Single 9-bar trace, one window (15-95 s); a 4-parameter flexible cubic reaches ~0.096 g/s, so the RMSE gap shows time-variation is needed, not that a particular mechanism is identified.
validity_range: One rig; the machine-null is on Foster's fitted trace, the ladder on the Waszkiewicz 9-bar rising-flow window.
primary_caveat: Sufficient, NOT unique: do not say 'dissolution caused the rising flow'. A flow curve becomes informative only with more observables and controlled perturbations.
practical_implication: Do not diagnose swelling/channeling from a dip-and-recovery alone; log pressure, flow, first-drip time, mass, control mode, and ideally timed TDS fractions.
reproduction: python -c "from puckworks.harness import kappa_t_ladder as f; print(f())"

dependencies.role: the bed-side temporal branch scored in the ladder

evidence.scope: Mass flow Q(t) at 9 bar vs time (long-run mean g/s and Pearson correlation, t>=15 s).
Steady-state basket-pressure vs mass-flow curve; recovered calibration parameters P_c, Q_c.

dependencies.role: the machine-and-wetting branch that reproduces a dip without any extraction-driven bed process

evidence.scope: Wetting-front depth s(t) and headspace height H(t) (mm) over the shot, vs the paper's fitted ODE curves and vs digitized CT measurements.
Normalized bed flow Q/Qm = min(Q_p, f(H,s))/Q_m vs experiment time.
Two scalar times (s): ponding time t_p and saturation time t_s, model-computed vs the authors' reported values.

dependencies.role: scores every branch on one window and returns the ladder
the measured flow trace all branches are scored against

evidence_selections.claim_observable: mass flow Q(t) at 9 bar over the scored window
evidence_selections.rationale: The bed-side temporal branch whose reconstruction error this claim reports, scored on exactly the observable named. EXCLUDED: gate_waszkiewicz_static_refit, which concerns the steady-state pressure-flow curve and the recovered P_c/Q_c -- a different observable.

evidence_selections.claim_observable: whether a mid-shot flow minimum can arise from machine and wetting response alone: the reproduced ponding and saturation times, AND the normalized flow curve in which the dip appears
evidence_selections.claim_domain: the Foster apparatus, its reported scalar times, and its normalized bed-flow curve
evidence_selections.rationale:
Fifth review P0-1. This selection previously named ONLY the supported scalar-times gate and deliberately excluded `gate_foster_fig15_flowmin` -- the NEGATIVE record covering the normalized flow curve -- on the ground that the claim 'asserts nothing about those observables'. But the claim asserts a DIP-AND-RECOVERY SHAPE, and the flow curve is precisely the observable that shape lives on. Selecting a related-but-different observable because the directly relevant record is unfavourable is the exact failure mode this architecture exists to prevent, and it had occurred here.

The flow-minimum record is now SELECTED and carries its negative outcome. The two scalar times are reproduced; the published normalized flow curve is NOT, so what this claim licenses is the structural capacity of a machine-and-wetting model to produce a dip-and-recovery, not a quantitative reproduction of the source's curve. `gate_foster_ct_trajectory` remains excluded on its own merits: it concerns wetting-front depth s(t) and headspace H(t), which this claim does not mention.

evidence_profile.scope: Mass flow Q(t) at 9 bar vs time (long-run mean g/s and Pearson correlation, t>=15 s).
Normalized bed flow Q/Qm = min(Q_p, f(H,s))/Q_m vs experiment time.
Two scalar times (s): ponding time t_p and saturation time t_s, model-computed vs the authors' reported values.

public_question: How can an exciting result weaken when the target variable and its uncertainty are audited?
headline: We thought a model had explained the fine-grind espresso dip — then we checked the units and the raw replicates.
plain_language_finding: After rebuilding the target as a coherent TDS-derived extraction yield (an earlier version mixed mg solute masses with g TDS), the raw measured cells are ORDERED across dial (18.27 -> 19.38 -> 19.62%), with the middle dial BELOW the coarse one — no interior 'fine-grind' maximum. A channeling model can still MAKE such a bump, but that is model capacity, not identification: the bump is fragile and smaller than the shot-to-shot spread.
uncertainty_or_sensitivity: Welch 95% CI on the middle-vs-coarse contrast excludes zero; the model's interior bump is near-flat at 9 bar and appears in only a minority of the closure grid — smaller than replicate spread. Means are described as ORDERED, not 'statistically monotone' (the 1.4-vs-1.7 interval includes zero).
validity_range: Schmieder E65S grinder DoE, fixed central flow/temperature condition; TDS-derived EY observable.
primary_caveat: These are Schmieder E65S grinder-DIAL positions — a dial number is NOT a particle size and is non-portable to another grinder without a calibrated adapter. Do not read a universal 'too-fine optimum'. Also: static channeling remains a viable GENERATOR (model capacity), the data just do not identify it as the cause.
practical_implication: Plot raw replicates before trend lines, use a coherent yield measure, and distinguish a machine-specific dial position from a physical grind characteristic.

dependencies.role: locates the interior maximum in the source response surface
compares the modelled and measured magnitudes
tests whether the interior maximum survives the channeling account
the fitted response-surface coefficients the vertex is read from

public_question: Can two individually plausible espresso components be combined safely just by sharing one state variable?
headline: Adding a swelling branch made this tested model worse.
plain_language_finding: A time-varying extraction model followed the rising flow trace much better than a constant baseline. But when a swelling branch was added through one shared porosity state, that state over-closed and the composite prediction became worse than the constant. The result rejects this composition, not swelling physics in general.
uncertainty_or_sensitivity: Over the 15-95 s window the composite 0.648 g/s is 1.13x the best-constant null (0.573 g/s) and 5.59x the extraction-only rung (0.116 g/s, cross-checked by degeneracy_rmse); the shared porosity over-closes to 0.0998 (below the 0.17 reference). A diagnosed mis-scale, reported not tuned away.
validity_range: 9-bar Waszkiewicz trace; the imported swelling parameters are mo2023_2's, applied to a saturated pre-wet rig; one observation operator.
primary_caveat: Diagnoses THIS shared-porosity composition, not the existence of swelling; does NOT prove the extraction-only mechanism; and 'simple is always best' is NOT the lesson — complexity is justified when it beats the baseline. Not coupled into the Guided Espresso Pull.
practical_implication: Do not assume a more elaborate model is more trustworthy; a simple baseline must stay visible and be beaten before components are combined through a shared state.

dependencies.role: the composition under test; adding the swelling branch is what worsens it

evidence.scope: Minimum composite porosity (eps_min vs eps0) and the 9-bar Q(t) RMSE vs the measured Waszkiewicz trace (g/s).
Mass flow Q(t) at 9 bar vs the measured Waszkiewicz trace over the 15-95 s saturated window (RMSE, g/s).
Structural identity of the coupled model's extraction-only Phi(t)/Q(t) closure to the standalone poroelastic component (a code property).

dependencies.role: the imported branch whose parameters are used unrefitted

evidence.scope: Mean yield (%) over the M_c 18-32 g window, across q (2 vs 4 mL/s) and across powders E/M/F at matched q.
Per-powder relative error between the recomputed CK k0 and the tabulated Table 2 k0 (m^2).
Fixed-dp flow-decay ratio q(60s)/q(0) (dp/mu/L cancelled) per powder E/H/M/F, plus the scalar s_m.
End-of-shot yield (fraction of extractable inventory) with swelling on vs off at q=2/3/4 mL/s (fixed-q), contrasted with the fixed-dP Carman-Kozeny flow-decay ratio.

dependencies.role: computes the composite and extraction-only residuals
the measured trace the composite is scored against

evidence_selections.rationale: The claim is ABOUT this composition's failure and this record diagnoses it on exactly that observable. EXCLUDED: the degeneracy reconstruction and reduction records, which establish the extraction-only closure's structural identity -- not what is asserted here.

evidence_selections.claim_observable: the effect of the imported swelling branch on end-of-shot yield at fixed flow
evidence_selections.claim_domain: the source's q = 2/3/4 mL/s fixed-flow conditions
evidence_selections.rationale: The imported branch is the subject under test. EXCLUDED: gate_mo2_fixed_flow_trends and gate_mo2_swelling_flow_decay, which carry NEGATIVE outcomes on yield trends and flow decay. Those are genuine limitations of the source port, preserved in the inventory, but they are not the observable this claim asserts.

public_question: Can a model match the final cup while leaving its hidden rate and inventory unresolved?
headline: The final cup can hide very different extraction clocks.
plain_language_finding: Across the tested endpoint data, many inventory-rate combinations fit nearly equally well (log-parameter SSE-Hessian condition number ~1,930; the 10%-near-optimal rate set covers ~76% of the tested grid). Held-out cup predictions remain reasonably stable, but the mechanistic model (8.2% MAPE) barely improves on a level-only constant (8.6%) and is worse on 50 of 108 held-out points. Timed fractions preserve rate information the final cup discards.
uncertainty_or_sensitivity: Practical (not structural) non-identifiability; no likelihood/noise model. The tested rate range is RIGHT-CENSORED at its upper edge. The inverse-curvature coupling is objective-surface geometry, NOT a statistical parameter correlation; the 10% set is a tested-domain threshold set, NOT a confidence interval.
validity_range: One model refit to one independent campaign; conditional on the tested model, observation operator, data, objective, and matched-endpoint domain.
primary_caveat: Endpoint prediction stability is NOT parameter identification and NOT mechanistic validation; the mechanistic model barely beats a level-only null. Not a claim of structural identifiability, and not evidence the mechanism transferred.
practical_implication: To learn mechanism, preserve the clock (collect timed fractions), measure the soluble inventory independently, and beat a simple level-only null before crediting a mechanism from endpoint accuracy.

dependencies.role: the extraction model, refitted to the target campaign for this claim

evidence.scope: Per-solute MAPE (%) between simulated and measured fraction concentrations over 15 experiments x 6 time-fraction windows.

dependencies.role: the whole-cup endpoint concentrations the profile is fitted to
profiles the inventory-rate objective and reports the near-optimal set
scores the cross-grind prediction against the level-only null

evidence_selections.claim_observable: per-solute fraction concentrations reconstructed by the extraction model
evidence_selections.claim_domain: the source campaign's 15 experiments x 6 time points
evidence_selections.rationale: The reconstruction underlying the claim's contrast between extraction clocks. It is a post-fit SAME-DATA record, which is precisely why the derived badge is RECONSTRUCTED and not PREDICTED.

evidence_profile.scope: Per-solute MAPE (%) between simulated and measured fraction concentrations over 15 experiments x 6 time-fraction windows.
